what_it_does: GPUs have several layers of on-chip fast memory (caches) arranged from fastest-but-tiny to slower-but-larger. When the first-level cache (L1D) misses, it currently checks a 'victim cache' — a small buffer holding recently evicted data — only as a secondary fallback, which adds latency. HIVE proposes making the victim cache a higher-priority destination: memory requests are routed to it before the main L1D cache for certain access patterns, so frequently needed data can be found faster. The paper reports reduced memory-access latency for memory-intensive workloads, though the abstract provides limited quantitative detail.
